title: Hearing
description: A single hearing's record in the five-hearing adversarial workflow (see workflows/five-hearing-adversarial.md) or a legal-moot single pass. This is what makes 'hearing memory' real rather than asserted: hearing N+1's agents are isolated fresh contexts (see AGENTS.md's independence rule) and can only know what a prior hearing found by reading this record - there is no other channel. Stored at matters/<ID>/moot/hearing-<n>.json (or hearings/ if a matter adopts that subdirectory name instead - see skills/legal-work/SKILL.md).

issues_addressed.description: issue_id values from issue.schema.json this hearing actually engaged with

repairs_required.description: What the case theory must fix before the NEXT hearing - this is the field that makes hearing memory real. The next hearing's agents read this list before starting, and re-litigating a repaired point without addressing the repair is what 'five identical arguments is a failure' (workflows/five-hearing-adversarial.md) actually means in a checkable sense.

disposition.description: The simulated decision-maker's ruling for this hearing - may go against the user, see agents/judiciary/ROLE.md
